transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-03 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Ivy (Redwood CSM), Lena (Scoutline CTO), Raj (ML Eng), Aisha (PM), Tom (Infra)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick roll call?
[00:11] Lena: Lena here, hi.
[00:13] Raj: Raj on my side.
[00:15] Aisha: Aisha, yep.
[00:17] Tom: Tom here.
[00:19] Maya: great, thanks. So agenda is pretty straightforward — scope the POC, confirm success criteria, sizing, and runnable bench plan. I'll hand off to Daniel for the tech bits in a sec.
[00:32] Daniel: cool thanks Maya. Quick context: Scoutline's been doing on-prem inference today via a mix of CPU+occasional GPU, right? Tom, is that still accurate?
[00:40] Tom: yeah we've been running smaller transformer retreival + a couple of fine-tuned LLM endpoints on a handful of VMs, but latency is all over the place and cost is spiking when QPS rises. 
[00:50] Maya: and your main ask is to evaluate Redwood for a 6-week pilot to validate unit economics and latency at scale?
[00:56] Lena: exactly. We need a clear per-token run-rate, and we want to know how batching and the KV cache will move the needle. Also security — we need audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:08] Daniel: good. High-level POC model we're proposing: 4-week technical run + 2-week validation/analysis. We run a baseline where we replay your traffic and synthetic variants, capture p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and throughput headroom. For the baseline we'll test hosted first then a dedicated pool if the numbers require it.
[01:26] Raj: can you define baseline metrics? like what numbers you'll report?
[01:30] Daniel: yes. We'll report: p50/p95 token-level latency, tokens/sec throughput, effective per-token cost (including batching overhead), cache hit rate and effective token reduction from KV prefix caching, and GPU utilization breakdown per model. Also attempt different quantization profiles — 8-bit and 4-bit where supported — and show impact on latency/cost/quality.
[01:47] Aisha: on quality, what regressions do you check? we can't degrade answer quality beyond a threshold.
[01:51] Daniel: we'll run your evaluation set — you provide ~500 prompts with ground truth or manually graded outputs. We'll compute top-level metrics like exact-match for retrieval, and a human sample for generation quality. If quality delta > 3% (we can define metric) then we stop the aggressive quantization path.
[02:08] Lena: sounds reasonable. Budget-wise, we have runway constraints. Our internal bar is less than $0.0009 per token average across a month if we move to production. Is that plausible?
[02:18] Maya: depends on ceiling. For hosted with aggressive batching and KV caching you can sample as low as $0.0004/token for batched long-sequence scenarios, but for low-latency single-turn chat it can be $0.0012/token or higher without dedicated capacity. The POC will narrow that.
[02:34] Tom: clarify batching — what latency tradeoffs are we talking about?
[02:38] Daniel: our runtime uses continuous batching. If you allow up to ~30ms of queuing, throughput increases and per-token cost drops significantly. For Scoutline's traffic mix — you said 60% short queries, 40% long— we expect a sweet spot with max batch delay 25-40ms to keep p95 under 150-200ms for most requests.
[02:56] Raj: our SLO target is p95 < 150ms for the search+generate path. Can Redwood hit that with batching?
[03:02] Daniel: yes for short tokens, with a dedicated pool and KV cache enabled we can target p95 ~120-140ms for 90% of traffic. Long-form generation >512 tokens will pull p95 up, but caching reduces repeated prefix cost.
[03:15] Aisha: tell me about KV cache — TTL, eviction, and how it reduces tokens.
[03:19] Daniel: KV cache stores recent prefixes per-customer or per-session. For a QPS with many repeated prefixes (e.g., system prompt + user context), we often see 20-40% token reduction on re-runs. TTL is configurable — in the POC we typically use 30 minutes to start, test effects at 5m/30m/24h. Eviction is LRU per host, and we can scope to namespace so customer data isn't mixed.
[03:42] Maya: also note for security we can integrate your KMS for key wrapping and we push audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3 — Tom you asked about compliance?
[03:51] Tom: yes SOC2 is a must, and we need to keep logs for 90 days. Also SSO/SAML for console access.
[03:59] Ivy: we have a SOC2 + support for external KMS; we'll share our security pack after the call.
[04:04] Lena: good. Back to cost modeling — show me an example breakdown for a sample workload.
[04:08] Daniel: sure. Hypothetical: 1M requests per month, average 60 tokens/req -> 60M tokens. If hosted average cost is $0.0008/token -> that's $48k/month. If we enable batching and caching that reduces effective tokens by say 30% and we use dedicated capacity discounts, you could get down to $0.00045/token -> $27k/month. We'll produce a sensitivity table in the report.
[04:29] Raj: what's included in the per-token number? is that infra only? or does it include model weights hosting?
[04:34] Maya: per-token in our reports includes runtime execution, GPU time amortized, network egress where applicable, and Redwood platform oversight. For dedicated there's a reserved capacity fee amortized across tokens — we'll show both raw runtime unit cost and the full landed per-token.
[04:48] Aisha: what assumptions do you make about concurrency and burst?
[04:51] Daniel: we model average QPS distribution and 95th percentile burst. For pilot we need your qps histogram. Absent that we use synthetic: base qps 50, spikes to 200 for 30s, sustained peaks of 100 for 5 mins. That drives autoscale/burst policy planning.
[05:07] Lena: schedule—what's the timeline if we sign POC?
[05:10] Maya: proposed: week 0 (this week) alignment and sample collection; week 1 baseline replay on hosted; week 2 stress + quantization experiments; week 3 run dedicated nodes if needed and trial caching; week 4 collect results + tuning; week 5 analysis and ROI; week 6 decision/next steps. So 6 weeks total.
[05:29] Tom: what would dedicated nodes cost for the pilot? just a ballpark so we can pre-approve budget.
[05:33] Maya: pilot dedicated pool for 4 GPUs for a week is typically in the low five figures — we'd give an exact quote in the SOW. The point of pilot is to see if the unit economics improve enough to justify the dedicated cost.
[05:45] Raj: do you support quantization to 4-bit on our model family? we use a Mistral-like base with custom fine-tune.
[05:51] Daniel: we support 8-bit and experimental 4-bit paths for many open architectures; for fine-tuned models we'll need to run a smoke test to catch any quality regressions. If the model uses complex custom ops, we may need a short onboarding step.
[06:05] Aisha: success criteria — let's define explicit pass/fail for the POC.
[06:09] Maya: suggested success criteria: 1) cost: verified landed per-token <= $0.0009 for baseline production mix; 2) latency: p95 end-to-end for search+generate < 150ms for >=90% of requests; 3) quality: generation quality delta within agreed threshold (we'll define 2-3% metric); 4) ops: Redwood integrates with Scoutline KMS + audit log pipeline; 5) runbook: documented autoscale and fallback policy. If we meet 4/5 with no critical security gaps, pilot is a go.
[06:36] Lena: we want an explicit rollback plan in case of regression post-rollout.
[06:40] Ivy: we'll include a fallback to hosted smaller model variant and automatic circuit-breaker in the deployment config so you can fail back to a safe baseline.
[06:48] Raj: about dataset rehearsal — we have dynamic retrieval that appends external docs often. How do you handle cache invalidation?
[06:55] Daniel: cache keyed by prompt hash + retrieval fingerprint. If your retrieval corpus mutates you control TTL or explicit invalidation API calls. We recommend short TTLs for highly dynamic content plus targeted invalidation after content updates.
[07:08] Tom: network topology — if we run private deployment in our VPC during pilot, will that affect latency?
[07:13] Daniel: private deployment in VPC has minimal network delta inside the region; the main latency delta is model cold-start and host sizing. We'll benchmark both hosted (region) vs private VPC to show delta.
[07:25] Lena: any potential gotchas?
[07:27] Daniel: a few: 1) tokenization mismatch between your preprocessing and our serving tokenizer can skew token counts; 2) extremely high variance prompts hurt batching efficiency; 3) some custom ops can block low-bit quant paths. We'll surface these during baseline.
[07:44] Maya: okay let's confirm what we need from Scoutline to kick off: 1) 500-1000 representative prompts, labeled by expected response length and priority; 2) qps histogram for last 30 days; 3) sample model artifact or specs (base + finetune); 4) security contacts for KMS + SIEM ingestion.
[08:03] Raj: we can provide those by Thursday.
[08:05] Maya: great. Daniel, for synthetic baseline can you outline the bench plan you'll run?
[08:10] Daniel: yes. Step A run: replay exact prompts at live token pace to get raw p50/p95 on hosted. Step B: synthetic batching window sweep (0-50ms) to measure cost/latency tradeoffs. Step C: enable KV cache with TTLs 5m/30m/24h to measure hit rates. Step D: quant evaluation 8-bit then 4-bit on small subset and quality checks. Step E: if dedicated approved, repro run on dedicated pool and compare. We'll produce a spreadsheet with cost model sensitivity and a slide deck.
[08:41] Aisha: for the quant experiments, will you include human-in-the-loop checks?
[08:44] Daniel: yes we'll sample 50 outputs per condition and score them. We usually ask customers to join a 2-hour quality review at the end of week 2.
[08:53] Lena: who owns the data movement? we have PII sometimes and would prefer no offsite copies.
[08:59] Maya: for sensitive data we can run the pilot fully in your VPC/private deployment or with hosted but with on-the-fly streaming and no retention. We'll sign an NDA addendum and use customer KMS.
[09:10] Tom: can you push logs to our S3? that's preferred.
[09:13] Ivy: yes we support S3 delivery for audit logs; we'll share the spec.
[09:16] Raj: I want to better understand the per-token math. earlier you said $0.00045/token with caching — can you show a worked example?
[09:23] Daniel: quick worked example in call: assume raw token execution cost on GPU = $0.0009/token single-shot. Batching improves GPU utilization and reduces per-token compute by 30% -> $0.00063. KV cache reduces average effective tokens by 35% -> effective per-token = $0.00063 * 0.65 = $0.00041. Add platform amortized fee 10% -> $0.00045. Dedicated discount can shift the base compute to $0.0006/token before batching. We'll provide that table.
[09:52] Aisha: for budgeting we need monthly run-rates across a range of 100k, 1M, 5M requests. Can you provide that?
[09:58] Maya: yes we'll include a tiered cost model in the SOW.
[10:01] Lena: one more question — SLA expectations for dedicated vs hosted?
[10:05] Maya: hosted has a platform SLA for uptime and best-effort latency SLAs; dedicated comes with an SLA-backed latency and uptime target in enterprise contracts. We'll include target numbers in the SOW.
[10:15] Daniel: quick note on observability — Console will give you token-level breakdown, model route latency, trace IDs and a per-route cost dashboard so you can attribute spend.
[10:26] Raj: useful. Also can we test a fallback flow that uses a smaller cheap model if latency spikes?
[10:30] Daniel: absolutely, automatic fallback to a cost-optimized model variant is part of our routing policies; we can test that in the POC.
[10:37] Maya: ok wrapping up—recap of next steps: Scoutline to share prompts, qps histogram, model spec by 2026-03-05; Redwood to run baseline and share results by 2026-03-06; Redwood to deliver draft SOW and pricing 2026-03-10; Plan bench week of 2026-03-16 if pilot approved.
[10:56] Lena: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[10:59] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[11:03] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contained slight mis-hearings — e.g., "K-V cash" heard once in the auto-transcript which is actually KV cache. Several speaker attributions were manually cleaned but some timestamps may shift by a few seconds. Links shared during call: https://drive.redwood.com/scoutline/poc-templates (deck), https://sheets.redwood.com/bench-results-template (cost model).
